feeds.title: What's Your Grief Blog
feeds.description: To put it simply, this website is about grief. Our mission is to promote grief education, exploration, and expression in both practical and creative ways.

feeds.title: Grief Healing
feeds.description: This blog is designed and intended to share any useful, accurate and reliable information about care giving, loss, grief and transition.

feeds.title: Let's Talk About Loss Blog
feeds.description: Beth French set up Let's Talk About Loss after she lost her mum when she was 20. Her grief made her feel lonely and confused, so she set up Let's Talk About Loss to create a space where grief wasn't a taboo subject. Let's Talk About Loss supports young people aged 18-35 who are bereaved. Whoever you've lost, we are a safe space to talk about that loss in a fun, relaxed environment.

feeds.title: The Grief Recovery Method Blog
feeds.description: The Grief Recovery Method blog provides articles and stories to help in the grieving process. The Grief Recovery Institute is an international non-profit organization that provides grief recovery assistance to people of all races, religions and backgrounds.

feeds.title: First Hour Grief Response Blog
feeds.description: First Hour Grief Response, Inc. is a support organization founded with the desire to provide hope and guidance on situation when there is a personal loss of a close loved one. This blog provides support and clarity on a number of issues and challenges faced by people during loss and hopes to connect together a community of similarly supportive people.

feeds.title: Renaissance Funeral Home » Grief
feeds.description: This section features articles on grief. Renaissance Funeral Home is the ultimate provider of creating healing experiences in the community.

feeds.title: Loving and Living Your Way Through Grief
feeds.description: Hi! I'm Emily Thiroux Threatt. I use writing to help friends deal with grief. I spend my time now writing and teaching others to write to deal with all kinds of losses. My passions are ceramics, acting, directing, designing, weaving, quilting, and cooking, especially vegan, and I am a certified vegan Chef.

feeds.title: Grief Refuge Blog
feeds.description: Grief Refuge is the best mobile app to help you cope with the loss of a loved one. Filled with insight and wisdom for managing grief, it helps you understand what to do with your loss: physically, emotionally, socially, and Spiritually.

feeds.title: Center for Grief and Trauma Therapy Blog
feeds.description: Read blog posts by our grief and trauma expert therapists providing hope, perspective, specific practices and education. The Center for Grief and Trauma Therapy started in 2019 because our founder, Dr Christina Zampitella, realized there was a need for specialist therapy services for the bereaved. Our professional team specializes in grief, loss, and trauma.

feeds.title: Griefline
feeds.description: Tips, tools and articles to help you manage grief and loss. Griefline has been serving the community for more than 30 years. We support Australians in their grief by providing space to be heard without judgement or labels and offering hope and healing after loss.

feeds.title: Lisa Appelo » Grief
feeds.description: I'm Lisa. I'm a recent widow and single mom to seven amazing children, here I share all of the good lessons God is teaching as He is so true and faithful to us.

feeds.title: Modern Loss Blog
feeds.description: Modern Loss is a place to share the unspeakably taboo, unbelievably hilarious, and unexpectedly beautiful terrain of navigating your life after death. Read personal essays from diverse people who have experienced all kinds of loss.

feeds.title: Grief Stories Blog
feeds.description: At Grief Stories, we passionately believe sharing stories and insights fosters connection, helping people to cope with grief. Health care experts and guests write insightful blog posts about the experience of grief and supporting bereaved people after a loss. We offer a range of resources to help grievers explore and express their own grief stories, and to connect with the stories of others.

feeds.title: Widow's Voice Blog
feeds.description: Soaring Spirits builds community. We create & maintain, innovative peer-based grief support programs for widowed men & women that serve a worldwide population.

feeds.title: Mark Liebenow - Grief (formerly Widowers Grief)
feeds.description: Mark Liebenow writes about grief, nature, and the wisdom of fools.

feeds.title: AfterTalk
feeds.description: We created AfterTalk as a place for Comfort and Sharing for those who have experienced loss or are supporting a Loved One in Hospice Care.

feeds.title: Faith & Grief
feeds.description: You will find stories of people's grief journeys and we hope you find comfort and connection through their experiences. We are a multi-faith non-profit whose mission is to provide opportunities for comfort & hope to those who have experienced the death of a loved one.

feeds.title: Everyone Dies (Every1Dies)
feeds.description: A thoughtful exploration of everything about life-limiting illness, dying, and death. Everyone Dies is a nonprofit organization with the goal to educate the public about the processes associated with dying and death, empower regarding options and evidence-based information to help them guide their care, normalize dying, and reinforce that even though everyone dies, first we live, and that every day we are alive is a gift.

feeds.title: Hope Again Blog
feeds.description: Hope Again is the youth website of Cruse Bereavement Support. It has been created for young people, by young people. We offer support, advice and a type of signposting service, solely online to children and young people who have lost a loved one/s. We want to break the isolation that grief brings, by providing a space for young people to explore their grief and feel less alone.

feeds.title: Grief and Sympathy Blog
feeds.description: Grief and Sympathy - a healing hug in times of grief and loss. Find comfort and advice, and get news and tips from the Grief and Sympathy website.

feeds.title: Elaine Mansfield Blog
feeds.description: Elaine Mansfield writes with a strong sense of place and an intimate connection to nature in her forthcoming memoir. Her writing reflects her 40 years as a student of Jungian psychology, mythology, philosophy, and meditation. Elaine facilitates bereavement support groups for people who have lost spouses or partners.

feeds.title: May Your Laughter Live
feeds.description: May You Laughter Live refers to the loss of my son. With personal examples, I give empathy, support, encouragement & advice to other parents to help them navigate this most difficult grief journey.

feeds.title: Good Grief!
feeds.description: So Good Grief! started by Margaret is a place to come to and cocoon for a while. It's a place to get ideas, find information and share stories, before moving back out into the busy world again. It's not meant to be a place that gets you stuck in grief but one that helps you to move on.

feeds.title: Widow's Christian Place
feeds.description: You're not alone. Here's a safe place, a growing place, a way out of the shadows of grief. This blog provides resources and Biblical direction for helping you trust Jesus through one of life's most difficult challenges.

feeds.title: Grounded Grief Therapy Blog
feeds.description: Hi! I'm Katherine Hatch. I am a grief and trauma therapist working with people. As a therapist, I am a companion and a witness. I will never fully understand the grief that any one person experiences because grief is so personal and individual. Yet I will be by your side, offering some structure, some guidance, some tools, and some wisdom that I have gathered from the countless stories of those who I have been with on this journey.

feeds.title: A Widow's Walk
feeds.description: I'm Margie and I lost my husband of 34 years, John, to the deadliest form of brain cancer, glioblastoma multiform (GBM) exactly 3 months after he had a grand mal seizure and a stage 4 tumor was discovered on his left frontal lobe. Welcome to my blog. I hope that sharing my story helps me and others reach a deeper and healthier understanding of grief.

feeds.title: Grief Counseling and Therapeutic Services, LLC Blog
feeds.description: Julie Bockenstedt, PhD, LISW, LCSW started Grief Counseling & Therapeutic Services, LLC when she noticed a lack of specialized grief services in the Quad Cities. She recognizes the special needs of those who are grieving. In this blog, we continue discussing the grief journey. We talk about coping, self-care, and other ways of managing our grief.

feeds.title: Inner Harbor
feeds.description: Inner Harbor is dedicated to supporting grieving students in schools and on college campuses across the country. The blog is an effort to bring awareness and normalization to young adult grief. We talk about death, the pandemic, suicide, and many other topics related to young, grieving adults.

feeds.title: What to Say When Someone Dies
feeds.description: Hi! I'm Teresa TL Bruce. I'm a widow, but that's not all I am. I'm a freelance proofreader, editor, and writer. My goal with this blog is to build a bridge of understanding between those who grieve and those who wish to help them. By sharing what I've learned since my husband's death and after other losses*, I hope to alleviate some of the bruising on those left behind by the Reaper's touch.

feeds.title: Wild Grief Blog
feeds.description: At Wild Grief, we merge peer support with the healing power of nature. By offering free, outdoor experiences for teens, young adults, families, and all-ages groups, we help more people find a place where they can remember, process and discover a path to healing.

feeds.title: Still Standing Magazine
feeds.description: Founded in 2012, Still Standing Magazine has been the world's leading online voice in breaking the silence on child loss - from conception to adulthood, and infertility. We share stories from around the world of writers surviving the aftermath of loss and grief - and include information on how others can help.

feeds.title: Jo Betz Grief Blog
feeds.description: Jo wrote Grief is a guided journal for those wishing to explore their grief after the death of a loved one through writing. Whether their loss was six months ago, or six years, the journal is a safe space to journal on a variety of topics. From the stages of grief, connection and anger, to loneliness, gratitude, regret and more, guided writing prompts are provided.

feeds.title: Goodgrief App Blog
feeds.description: The Goodgrief App is the social network for loss where grieving people can privately connect, chat, and support each other in finding a new normal. Goodgrief works by putting you in touch with others who lost their spouse, parent, sibling, child, relative, or friend due to a variety of causes.

feeds.title: Young, Widowed & Dating Blog
feeds.description: I'm Kerry Phillips. Though I'll forever grieve the loss of my hubby, the dark cloud has finally lifted and there are now more bursts of sunshine. Whether you've been widowed six months or six years, the grief and pain of losing a spouse or partner never goes away. Join me as I share my own story and those of others from the young and widowed community.

feeds.title: josiah+co. Blog
feeds.description: I am Melissa. My hope for this blog is to use it as a creative outlet as we walk through our miscarriage loss journey. I hope that along the way you can relate, gain some insight, learn how to support a friend, or learn how to better walk through the journey yourself. Here you'll find my raw thoughts, unfiltered; resources I've found helpful along the way.

feeds.title: The Grief Help Blog
feeds.description: The Grief Help Blog features articles, tips and exercises to help you cope with life after loss by Heather Stang and other esteemed grief professionals.

feeds.title: Grief to Gratitude Blog
feeds.description: Debbie is a psychotherapist in private practice in New York City. Her husband, Jim, died suddenly in her arms when she was only 36 years old. As a psychotherapist specializing in trauma, grief, and loss, her clinical training is steeped in Western traditions of healing. She helps normalize common feelings and experiences for people who are grieving and holds space for each of us to experience grief in our way and time because grief is not linear.
